# Actor Spring Boot Starter

> A Spring Boot starter that runs Pekko typed actors as Spring beans. Add `@EnableActorSupport`, implement `SpringActor` (or `SpringShardedActor` for cluster sharding), and use `SpringActorSystem` to spawn, look up and message actors. The public API has no Pekko types: use the starter's types, not raw Pekko or Akka APIs. It ships as `io.github.seonwkim:actor-spring-boot-starter` (add `actor-spring-boot-starter-cluster` for cluster mode), needs Java 21+ and Spring Boot 3.5+, and is configured with typed `spring.actor.*` properties.

The full text of the Getting Started page and every guide, with code inlined, is in [llms-full.txt](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/llms-full.txt): read it when the links below are not enough.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/): what the starter is for and how actors fit into a Spring Boot application
- [Getting Started](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/getting-started/): dependencies for Gradle and Maven, `@EnableActorSupport`, and the first configuration
- [Migrating from 0.x](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/migrating-from-0x/): new coordinates, packages and APIs in 1.0, step by step

## Guides

- [Actor Registration and Messaging](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/actor-registration-messaging/): register actors as beans, spawn them, use tell and ask, timers, watching and message adapters
- [Pub/Sub Topics](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/pub-sub-topics/): one-to-many messaging where publishers do not know the subscribers
- [Routers](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/routers/): spread messages across a pool of worker actors
- [Receptionist](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/receptionist/): find actors by service key, once or by subscribing to changes
- [Dispatchers](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/dispatchers/): choose the threads an actor runs on, Spring executors and virtual threads
- [Logging with MDC and Tags](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/logging/): add MDC values and actor tags to log lines
- [Sharded Actors](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/sharded-actors/): one actor per entity ID, spread across a cluster
- [Cluster Formation](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/cluster-formation/): join a cluster through seed nodes, or find peers through a JDBC table, Redis or your own store without Kubernetes RBAC
- [Split Brain and Leases](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/split-brain-and-leases/): choose which side of a network split stays up, and keep singletons and shards on one node with a lease in a JDBC table, Redis or your own store
- [Replicated Data](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/replicated-data/): maps, counters and sets copied to every node, with local, majority or all consistency
- [Persistence with Spring Boot](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/persistence-spring-boot/): keep actor state with Spring Data and other Spring Boot tools
- [Event-Sourced Actors](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/event-sourcing/): store events instead of state with actor-persistence, recover after a restart, snapshots, journal tables on the application's DataSource
- [Projections](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/projections/): read the events of event-sourced actors into Spring Data or Spring Kafka, exactly once or at least once, resuming from a stored offset
- [Reactor Streams](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/reactor-streams/): a `Mono` of an ask, a `Flux` that feeds an actor with backpressure, and a `Flux` of the messages an actor sends (`actor-streams`)
- [Streaming to Clients](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/streaming-to-clients/): Server-Sent Events (Spring MVC or WebFlux), WebSocket (`ActorWebSocketHandler`) and gRPC (`ActorGrpc`) from actors; a client disconnect stops the actor-side subscription
- [Running in Production](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/production/): graceful shutdown, health checks, Kubernetes probes, cluster metrics, the actors endpoint and tracing across tell and ask
- [AI Agents](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/ai-agents/): one sharded actor per agent, supervised conversations, non-blocking model calls and rate limits
- [Testing](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/testing/): the `@ActorTest` slice, multi-node clusters in one JVM with `ActorCluster`, and the contract suites for your own `PeerRegistry` or `LeaseStore`

## Examples

- [Examples overview](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/): the runnable example projects in the repository and what each shows
- [Simple](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/simple/): basic actors in a single, non-clustered application
- [Cluster](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/cluster/): sharded actors across several cluster nodes
- [Synchronization](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/synchronization/): actor-based synchronization compared with locks and databases
- [Chat](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/chat/): a real-time chat built on pub/sub topics, with no extra middleware
- [Monitoring](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/examples/monitoring/): actor metrics through Micrometer without a Java agent (tags, overhead, the optional agent), exposed to Prometheus

## Reference

- [Configuration Reference](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/guides/configuration/): every configuration key the starter reads, with its default
- [Spring Conventions](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/contributing/spring-conventions/): how the starter compares with the conventions of other Spring projects
- [RFCs](https://seonwkim.github.io/actor-spring-boot-starter/contributing/rfcs/): design proposals for the starter's API and behaviour
